description:
fz-go4.18.4 deleted the seal, whose runtime-demand-frontier walk was the ONLY thing that analyzed and published Executable facts for LATENT executables (escaped/opaque callables reached only through the runtime-demand frontier, e.g. a lambda passed as a reducer). Two #[cfg(test)] observability paths depended on it:

1. fixture_facts::canonical_call_edge_facts + World::root_executable_frontier over a legacy full world.drive(). It now sees only the entry cone, so latent generated-lambda executables are invisible. Also feeds fixture_contract_harness_test semantic.activations/executables metrics.
2. The addressed-keying convergence observation (fz-y6w / fz-f98.14.10.2): asserts qsort/append collapse to one key, partition inputs fold, <=26 activations -- its substance is the analyzed-activation inventory that lived on the deleted seal's SemanticClosure.

Production is UNAFFECTED -- the product path discovers these executables via the RuntimeDemand product; the fixtures interp/compile correctly. Only legacy test-observability was removed with the seal.

IGNORED awaiting this ticket (each carries the record in its #[ignore] reason):
- fixture_facts_test::canonical_call_edge_facts_preserve_source_spans_and_hide_generated_ids
- drive_test::compiler2_quicksort_root_closes_with_a_finite_recursive_frontier

DONE = re-base the oracle (and these two tests) on a product-path activation inventory (drive to RootBackendProduct, read session.materialized_executables() -- same source Compiler2::emit_product_semantic_dumps uses), migrate fixture_contract_harness_test off root_executable_frontier, then delete the #[cfg(test)] World::root_executable_frontier legacy ambient-scan helper entirely.
title: Re-base fixture call-edge oracle + finite-frontier convergence observation onto product-path activation inventory
